newsitem.title: USA: U.S. opposes any renewal of aluminium pact.
newsitem.headline: U.S. opposes any renewal of aluminium pact.

text.p: The United States has no plans to take part in any renegotiation of a new Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) among aluminum producers, U.S. officials said Thursday.
A spokeswoman for Acting Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said speculation that some of the members of the original MOU had begun negotiations was unfounded.
"We have no plans of renegotiating," the spokeswoman said. "We have not heard of any other meetings," she added.
The U.S. Trade Representative's office agreed several weeks ago to a proposal to continue informally collecting data on aluminum production, a trade official said.

The 1994 MOU, which expired earlier this year, aimed to contain world aluminum stockpiles following the breakup of the Soviet Union. It was signed by Australia, Canada, the European Union, Norway, Russia and the United States.
The agreement drew criticism in the United States, especially from aluminum users, who said it caused prices to rise. It also prompted a Justice Department anti-trust probe.
Patricia Plunkert, an official at the U.S. Geological Survey, said moves were afoot to persuade the Russian industry to resume publishing production data.
"We are working with the Russians to get publication of the data going again," Plunkert added.
The MOU set up a working group with a representative from each signatory country to help compile aluminum production and export data. Publication of the data ended last December.

Plunkert, who is the U.S. representative on the working group, said Canadian officials, who published the compiled data on behalf of the MOU members, were due to meet soon with Russian officials to discuss resuming data publication.
She said figures for Russian production were not published separately, but were included as part of European production in the International Primary Aluminium Institute's (IPAI) data.
"As far as we are concerned, and I have talked to the Canadians, no one is talking about reinstating an MOU," Plunkert said.
